projectTitle: MerMAID - MerR-based Mercury Assay for In-field Detection
tagline: One mercury ion among a billion molecules of water - a living sensor that glows red, read by a portable detector fed by a modular sample-extraction platform.
summary: HongKong-JSS is a four-school joint team (Y.W.C.A. Hioe Tjo Yoeng College, Po Leung Kuk Celine Ho Yam Tong College, Pentecostal School, Yan Oi Tong Tin Ka Ping Secondary School) that built a complete mercury-screening system for agricultural water and soil: a MerR-regulated E. coli biosensor expressing mRFP1e, a portable modular fluorescence reader, and a motorised sample-extraction platform that turns soil and water into a standard assay input. They designed, built and tested 13 biosensor prototypes - 2 aptamer-based and 11 protein-based - of which two protein designs responded to Hg2+, with the best showing low background, a response down to about 1 ppb (0.005 uM, roughly sixfold below the WHO drinking-water guideline of 6 ug/L), no cross-response to Cd2+, Pb2+ or Zn2+ at the concentrations tested, and retained function after alginate encapsulation. It took 1st Runner-up Grand Prize in the High School section and won Best Village Project, and the reason is visible on every page: the wiki's standing rule is that every number carries its conditions and a source, and the team separates demonstrated results from deployment claims more rigorously than most university teams.
awards: Best Village Project winner (Agriculture / Food & Nutrition / Fashion & Cosmetics / Art & Design)

dry.frameworks: The headline model is a calibration-and-inverse-prediction framework rather than a mechanistic simulation, and it is unusually well executed. Image signals were defined explicitly before any fitting: colour response C = 1 - (G_pellet / G_white) from green-channel intensity measured in ImageJ on pellets photographed against a white tile, and fluorescence response F = R_pellet / R_background from red-channel intensity inside a light box, with the matched untreated control from the same run and timepoint subtracted (delta-C, delta-F) and no OD normalisation. They then fitted a log-linear model delta-S = A + b log10(c / 0.005 uM) with 0.005 uM chosen as the reference so A is directly interpretable, giving delta-C = 0.04363 + 0.07591 log10(c/0.005) and delta-F = 0.42290 + 1.08721 log10(c/0.005). Crucially, calibration and validation data were separated up front - 20 calibration measurements from four runs (2, 6, 8 and 13 October) and 10 held-out validation measurements from two further runs (14 and 15 October) for each readout, all at the four-hour timepoint across 0.005, 0.01, 0.03, 0.05 and 0.1 uM. The model was inverted to estimate unknown concentration, c-hat = 0.005 uM x 10^((delta-S - A)/b), and scored by RMSE on the held-out runs: approximately 0.0483 uM for colour and 0.0319 uM for fluorescence, with all numerical predictions included so that failures were not hidden (a 0.1 uM sample on 15 October was estimated at 0.246 uM by colour). On the hardware side they ran CAD-based dry-lab studies for a UV advanced-oxidation-process reactor, modelling fluid flow dynamics, UV photo-oxidation kinetics and lamp exposure times for both a batch quartz-tube reactor and a thin-layer millifluidic cassette, computing a residence time of 192.6 s and a modelled minimum-to-maximum light ratio of 92.2% across the 1 mm layer; the filter assembly was developed parametrically in OpenSCAD. Promoter selection also used in silico promoter-strength analysis, which predicted J23106 to be comparable to P429 and so added it as a comparison design.
dry.dataviz: Presentation is built around separating what was measured from what is assumed. Charts show individual run points alongside coloured means and error bars rather than only pooled summaries, the model page plots known versus estimated concentration against a dashed perfect-prediction line with out-of-calibration-range estimates marked separately, and tables consistently split 'experimental finding' from 'design goal' and 'prototype performance' from 'deployment claim'. Every figure caption states its conditions. The hardware readout itself is a data-visualisation artefact: Detection Unit V3.0 pairs a Hamamatsu C12880 miniature spectrometer (288-pixel detector, 340-850 nm, 12 nm typical FWHM) with two ESP32-S3-N16R8 microcontrollers driving a local TFT display and a Wi-Fi-connected web interface that shows the recorded spectrum and the raw signal at a user-selected target wavelength, with online data logging, registered devices, selected-wavelength trends and recorded runs reviewable on a phone or computer. A red/amber/green status display was added later, and the team deliberately separated device status, fluorescence reading, concentration estimate and safety judgement on screen so that a green operational light cannot be misread as 'this sample is safe'.
dry.datascience: The analysis is notable for publishing its own limitations as a work plan. They state that the pooled model does not separately estimate run-to-run variation, that the reported concentrations are point estimates with no uncertainty intervals, that no detection or quantification limit has been established, and that rounded signal values were used as fitting inputs. They then specify the fixes concretely: a random-intercept mixed model delta-S_ri = A + b log10(c_ri/0.005) + u_r + e_ri with run-specific slopes only if the data support them and with convergence and singularity checks; inverse-calibration intervals that distinguish prediction for a new run from prediction for a run containing a measured reference standard; a per-run intercept correction A_r = delta-S_standard,r - b log10(c_standard/0.005) estimated from a known standard run alongside every experiment; leave-one-run-out cross-validation over six folds with the warning that selecting and evaluating on the same cross-validation results produces optimistic estimates; and comparison of the local log-linear fit against a four-parameter logistic model if data across 0.001-5 uM becomes available. They also ran and reported an exploratory sensitivity check swapping calibration runs, and honestly noted that because the validation runs were examined during that comparison they no longer constitute a completely untouched final assessment. Results-page statistics use two-sided paired t-tests across five independent paired runs with explicit notice that p-values are unadjusted for the three readouts. Hardware performance was quantified the same way: automated water delivery gave a coefficient of variation of 1.95% against 7.41% across 10 manual syringe runs, drainage retained volumes of 0.28, 0.31 and 0.30 mL (mean ~0.30 mL, about 95% liquid recovery), and reducing tubing bore from 7 mm to 1 mm over a 10 cm segment was computed to cut geometric dead volume accordingly.
dry.software: Open hardware and firmware rather than a bioinformatics tool. The Detection Unit CAD is published in Onshape (https://cad.onshape.com/documents/2228cb45d05bdbc67479791d) and the firmware and software at https://github.com/hkjssplkchc2026/mercurysense, containing ESP32 firmware, the C12880 spectrometer driver, acquisition instructions and Python/web monitoring software, with a live monitoring web app for reviewing spectra and runs. The Extraction Unit code is at https://github.com/davidlueng986-alt/MerMAID-Extraction-Unit. An itemised bill of materials is published with a ~USD 357 core-component subtotal (LED 2x 560 nm at USD 2.60, etc.), and the team states plainly that this overshot the USD 40 affordability target stakeholders had asked for. The detection unit went through four versions (AS7343 14-channel spectral sensor in a laser-cut acrylic box, to an opaque 3D-printed enclosure with recessed lid and adjustable optical mounts, to the C12880 spectrometer with interchangeable filters, fluid handling and web interface) and the extraction platform through three, with state-machine control sequences published for the water, soil and UV-AOP modules together with error-handling tests covering pump timeouts, watchdog recovery, soil-mass checks, stirring feedback, reagent availability and weighing faults. An educational browser game, 'Small Signal: a MerMAID field school', is published as a 3-5 minute pixel-art laboratory game in which players build a biological signal path, compare an unknown sample with its controls, and decide what the evidence supports - and is labelled a beta prototype whose educational effectiveness has not yet been evaluated. Repository: https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/hongkong-jss.

good.publicEngagement: Nine targeted outreach events reaching over 2,400 participants, organised as an explicit four-tier framework. Tier 1 (primary students and parents, over 1,600 people) ran interactive Open Day and Information Day booths at Y.W.C.A. Hioe Tjo Yoeng College and Po Leung Kuk Celine Ho Yam Tong College with strawberry DNA extraction and live gel electrophoresis demonstrations. Tier 2 (over 730 secondary peers) covered Microbiology 101 for Grade 10 students on microbe handling, laboratory safety, cleanliness and contamination prevention, and a morning assembly for 700 Grade 7-12 students that framed synthetic biology through agricultural mercury contamination and explained how cellular components can be repurposed as logic gates and biosensors. Tier 3 is the most durable: a two-day Teacher Biotech Training Workshop for 30 local school teachers covering PCR and agarose gel electrophoresis, combined with a standing loan programme letting those teachers borrow DNA samples and laboratory equipment from the team - a deliberate attempt to leave teaching capacity behind after the competition ends. Tier 4 took the work into public and civic space: an exhibitor stand at InnoEX 2026, the international innovation and technology exhibition in Hong Kong, and a presentation alongside the Drainage Services Department at its Annual Media Briefing, which put the project on an official government webpage and into local news. They also ran a street interview with 30 members of the public specifically about a 'mercury-free' produce certification label, finding unanimous support for the idea, 14 people rating it very important for public health, 12 supporting it even at higher vegetable prices, 22 willing to buy certified produce at normal prices and 4 willing to pay extra - while also recording that 19 respondents remained somewhat or very worried about engineered bacteria leaking from the sealed device against only 8 who were not, a finding they published rather than buried. The browser game 'Small Signal' extends this by teaching the reasoning - compare the unknown against its controls, then decide what the evidence can support.
good.ihp: Human Practices ran on a stated operating principle - respond promptly to stakeholder feedback, and let it drive the next hardware revision - structured across four stages and a five-question cycle (Inspiration, Intercommunication, Investigation, Implementation, Impact) with the rule that each engagement must end in either a documented change or a documented reason for no change. There is also a five-tier Target User Prioritisation Pyramid which they explicitly label a working framework rather than a validated exposure ranking, and which puts underserved communities near suspected contamination sources such as informal e-waste processing sites above farmers, researchers, regulators and the general public. The traceable changes: the Drainage Services Department's guidance moved them off the chromoproteins used in earlier projects onto mRFP1e as a dual readout - visible colour for non-specialists plus a more sensitive fluorescence channel for quantification - and DSD, the Water Supplies Department and university researchers together pushed them to test lower concentrations, benchmark against international reference values, and assess cross-response to interfering heavy metals (hence the Cd2+/Pb2+/Zn2+ selectivity panel). Koo's Farm and local wet market vendors demanded numerical readings instead of qualitative colour indicators, which is the direct reason the AS7343 14-channel sensor was replaced by the wavelength-resolved Hamamatsu C12880 and why a numerical display and web readout exist. University professors said soil particulates must be removed before optical measurement and recommended a modular design, which produced the separate water, soil and planned organic-mercury extraction modules. Users reported excessive syringe force on the V1 filter stack (2 um pre-filter plus 0.45 um membrane), so manual syringe delivery was replaced by pump-driven dosing - measured as an improvement from 7.41% to 1.95% coefficient of variation. On-site trials at Blue Girl Organic Farm and Yeung Marine Products Limited with agricultural soil extracts, irrigation water and fish pond water (run without GM bacteria, since they could not legally be taken out of the lab) produced requests for clearer indicators and better protection against water and mud, answered with a red/amber/green status display, a reinforced housing, and maintenance access and modularity designed into the proposed V4.0. A second public survey combining street interviews with hands-on demonstrations for 195 people found 87.7% more confident that ordinary people could participate in checking soil and water safety and 84.1% finding the digital readout easy to understand - and the team immediately noted that perceived confidence and readability do not establish analytical accuracy, and separated device status from safety judgement in the interface as a direct result. More Happy Farm said plainly that not every farmer wants to own a device, which pushed them towards a service model. Throughout, they keep stating what their evidence does not cover: a response in a controlled biological assay does not establish accurate measurement in soil extracts, reliable operation of the complete device, or suitability for regulatory decisions.
good.realWorld: The commercial concept is Certification-as-a-Service rather than instrument sales: farmers pay an annual subscription, the team visits to test soil on site with MerMAID, passing farms receive a 'Heavy Metal-Free' certificate and logo for supermarket packaging that lets them command a premium, and random surprise re-tests throughout the year (affordable precisely because the test is cheap and fast) guard the certificate's integrity. The plan is backed by a SWOT matrix, a competitor comparison against off-site laboratory testing (HKD 500+ per test, weeks of turnaround) and quick chemical test strips, and a five-step business plan naming AFCD, the Hong Kong Organic Resource Centre and premium supermarkets as the partners whose endorsement would make the certificate a standard. What lifts it above a typical student business plan is the case-study section: they analyse three real commercial analogues - Hygiena's reader-plus-consumables-plus-records model, SGS's accredited food-safety testing service, and Hong Kong's AFCD/VMO Accredited Farm Scheme - and draw out the uncomfortable implications, including that MerR-responsive bioavailable Hg(II) and a reference method's total-mercury result may be different measurands that cannot be assumed to agree just because both are labelled mercury, that a logo on packaging cannot replace a sample-to-report record tied to farm, location, date, sample ID and method scope, and that the full cost per valid result must include consumables, controls, staff time, storage, failed runs and waste handling. They state outright that the USD 350 build cost missed the USD 40 target, that the certification journey is a proposed direction, that the current prototype does not establish that any farm or product is heavy-metal-free, and that they claim no certification authority. Real-world constraints are acknowledged rather than wished away: engineered microbes cannot legally be placed in bins or taken into the field in Hong Kong, the on-site demonstrations therefore ran without GM bacteria, and the sub-five-minute loading and readout sequence is distinguished from the five hours of reporter expression the actual assay needs.

gemsTakeaway: Adopt their calibration discipline wholesale: split runs into calibration and validation before fitting anything, subtract a control from the same run and timepoint, invert the fit to predict unknowns, report RMSE on the held-out runs with the failures left in, flag out-of-range estimates, and then publish the statistical work you have not done yet (run-aware mixed model, inverse-calibration uncertainty intervals, leave-one-run-out cross-validation, a per-run reference standard) as a named plan. The second lesson is their teacher-capacity play - training 30 local teachers in PCR and gel electrophoresis and lending them the reagents and kit - which multiplies a school team's reach far more cheaply than any one-off workshop.
